pr_title: domain, executor: fix sysvar cache race
pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/25272 close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/25781

Problem Summary:

This fixes a race condition in the sysvar cache whilch could lead to lost updates with sysvar changes.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

A bug in the sysvar cache identified by flaky test cases has been fixed.

The fix includes using a separate mutex to protect against concurrent rebuilding of the sysvar cache. I originally considered using the same `svc.Lock()`, but this would likely lead to performance regressions since calls to `GetGlobalVar()` might block waiting for longer.

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [ ] Unit test
- [ ] Integration test
- [ ] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No code

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
~Unfortunately this could lead to performance regressions because `GetGlobalVar()` checks if the cache needs rebuilding (`rebuildCacheIfNeeded()`). This requires a read-lock, which will block waiting for longer because the lock is now held while reading the data. If this becomes observable, we may need to change the design to use 2 locks: one to protect the structures svc.session / svc.global and one to protect against rebuilding the cache.~

**This has been fixed.** I added a new mutex to protect against concurrent rebuild instead.

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

Documentation

- [ ] Affects user behaviors
- [ ] Contains syntax changes
- [ ] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features
- [ ] Changes MySQL compatibility

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

```release-note
A race condition could occur in the sysvar cache that led to lost updates with the statement 'SET GLOBAL'.
```

> Is not there already `svc.Lock(); defer svc.Unlock()` several lines later? IMO, you either just lock `svc` at the beginning, or read lock first then write lock.

@xhebox it needs to be exclusive lock since a read lock won't prevent this scenario:
* Updated Request 1 starts, reads table tables.
* An update occurs, triggering an update to the table and update request 2 to start.
* Update request 2 updates the cache
* Update request 1 updates the cache

I originally moved the `svc.Lock()` to earlier, but abandoned this approach because of the comment under "Performance regression" in the issue description.

> I don't know if it makes sense to linearize `RebuildSysVarCache` if it is async by design. But, it looks good to me.

Medium-term it would be better to separate the rebuilding of cache from a notification event to rebuilding it as part of a recurring process. i.e. you can skip the recurring rebuilds if the cache was rebuilt recently, but you can't skip the notification events.

I looked into this for https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/24700 (since there should be some framework to observe these jobs and measure their run time, memory usage etc. It makes sense to add skipping the recurring rebuild straight into the framework too). I haven't started it yet.

I believe I might have figured out the cause of this! It is in this function:
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/c70662bbecd0bd2a4db62e15bc0393f3aaf55906/domain/sysvar_cache.go#L112-L146

The Lock is only held when replacing the cache, not when reading the table values (`svc.fetchTableValues(ctx)`), so it's possible that the following can occur:

- Updated Request 1 starts, reads table tables.
- An update occurs, triggering an update to the table and update request 2 to start.
- Update request 2 updates the cache
- Update request 1 updates the cache

Thus the update request 2 is completely lost. We know that there are concurrent calls to `RebuildSysVarCache` (and there could be concurrent sysvar updates).

The fix is to hold the lock when reading the table values. This ensures updates are ordered and no requests are lost.

The only other possibility is that `GetGlobalVar` is failing, and the default is being substituted:
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/c70662bbecd0bd2a4db62e15bc0393f3aaf55906/session/session.go#L1118-L1129

But I don't think this is the case, since the line above (`select @@global.max_connections;`) is using exactly the same function call.

@tiancaiamao This is also used by https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/1e5000c631337629c268a317f06dfb4db956a49a/domain/sysvar_cache.go#L47-L58 which is part of the `SysVarCache` and can't call `domain.NotifyUpdateSysVarCache`.

I could add the channel to the `SysVarCache` instead of a mutex, but my hope is we figure this out better for https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/24700 so that the Loops backoff their regular execution when they are manually triggered.

review_comments: These two lines can be moved out of the lock scope.

@ngaut did you mean `newSessionCache` and `newGlobalCache`?

I had considered this, but my reason for keeping it protected by the lock is that:
1. The `RebuildSysVarCache` is called asynchronously.
2. The memory footprint will be more stable if concurrent requests don't allocate memory.

It is a small difference however, so I am of course happy to change it.
Yes, please. Make sure the lock scope is as small as possible. It is also more clear to avoid reader question why newSessionCache and newGlobalCache are protected by lock.
